trust_decision.summary: An untrusted (HTTP-uploaded) agent bundle may not declare server-side Python `callable:` tools that the runner imports and invokes; the decision is made inside the shared upload validator, gated on the same trust signal as the policy-handler allowlist (trusted single-user/local uploads keep the feature).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'Uploaded Agent Bundle', so an engineer looks first at the one shared validator for uploaded bundles; that is also the only place a bundle is parsed on the untrusted HTTP path.

fix_sites.entry_point: _is_dotted_callable_path helper (no direct public entry; consumed by the shared upload validator)
POST /v1/sessions (multipart bundle) and PUT /v1/sessions/{session_id}/agent reach it through validate_agent_bundle
the guard invocation inside validate_agent_bundle, used by sessions.py:11987, sessions.py:19411 and session_mcp_servers.py:204/237

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: omnigent/tools/local_callable.py:196-215 (LocalCallableTool lazily imports the spec's dotted path and invokes it in-process; registered via omnigent/tools/manager.py:739-756), separate from the sink named in the fix, omnigent/runner/tool_dispatch.py:565-614

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Trusted single-user/local uploads are explicitly exempt (enforce_handler_allowlist=False), so a solver can argue every already-validated or non-HTTP path (runner re-load, the AP in-process wrapper, sys_session_create relays) needs no second guard.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Bundled file tools (`tools/python/*.py`, `tools/typescript/*.ts`) are legitimate local tools whose LocalToolInfo.path also carries a path string; an over-broad fix that rejects every server-runtime tool with a path would break them. They must stay allowed while dotted import paths are rejected.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: omnigent/spec/parser.py:2517-2519 (file tools get bundle-relative paths), fix.diff:24-28 and fix.diff:173-189

O6_input_shapes: a plain dotted import string (`callable: subprocess.check_output`) in a single-file omnigent YAML
the same dotted callable declared in a sub-agent's tools, requiring recursion over spec.sub_agents
bundle-relative file tool paths containing '/' or ending .py/.ts, which must stay allowed
trusted local-server uploads (enforce_handler_allowlist=False), which must keep accepting callables

O7_producer.where: omnigent/spec/omnigent.py:465-522 resolves the YAML `callable:` string with importlib and omnigent/spec/omnigent.py:1936-1962 / :1965-2011 re-emit it as LocalToolInfo.path; omnigent/spec/parser.py:2491-2520 is the config.yaml producer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: re-apply the callable-tool rejection when the runner re-loads a stored bundle (the same load() call, prune_invalid_sub_agents=True)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the runner is where the import+invoke sink lives and already re-loads every bundle locally; a maintainer adding defence-in-depth or a later advisory could put the check here

O8b_injection_room.sibling: refuse dotted callable resolution for specs from session-scoped (untrusted) agents at dispatch time
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this is the sink the fix's own docstring names, and a sink-level guard is the obvious alternative to an upload-boundary guard

O8b_injection_room.sibling: filter omnigent-python-callable tools in the AP ToolManager registration
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a second registration point for the same spec field, in a different package, that a wrapper-level fix would naturally target

O8b_injection_room.sibling: reject dotted `callable:` paths at parse time unless a trusted flag is set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the parser already rejects '/' and '.py' paths here, so extending it is a plausible maintainer change

O9_family: CWE-94 code injection (authenticated runner RCE via untrusted agent-spec callable tools)

O10_build.toolchain: pyproject.toml (pip/uv install, optional dev extra), pytest with pytest-asyncio/xdist
O10_build.project_tests: tests/server/test_bundles.py exercises validate_agent_bundle directly (including the policy-callable alias test at tests/server/test_bundles.py:219); no route-level tests for PUT /sessions/{id}/agent were located in the time available

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject every server-runtime local tool that has a path (or gate only at _resolve_spec_callable), which either breaks bundled tools/python/*.py file tools or leaves sub-agent callables and the AP-side LocalCallableTool import path open.
